question: Geraghty (1983) Table 15 states the reflexes of Proto-Eastern Oceanic, which is not a node. Against what are the 38 communalects stated, and which lects carry them?
chosen_reading: Against Proto-Central Pacific (the user's comment on decision geraghty1983-communalects: 'listing them under PCP'), composed: PEO *nt, *nr, *ŋk, *q, *mw are PCP *d, *dr, *ɡ (q), *ʔ, *ŋʷ (gw); PEO *z is PCP *c and *z, which Geraghty (1986: 297) separates (s in Tubai, Nalea and Gone Dau is the reflex of *z; s elsewhere is *c under Eastern Fijian Apical Prenasalisation); the lexically conditioned kw, qw of 1983 are PCP *kw, *qw, and a communalect with 'no labiovelars' has the reflex of *k, *q for them. PEO *bw and *pw have no PCP counterpart and are stated against POc (parent_lect_id poc); PEO *R (zero everywhere) is not entered, since the row POc *R > ∅ stands on PCP. Environments are those of the key to sound changes (p. 186); a reflex that no numbered change accounts for has 'conditions unknown'. 37 dialects and Gone Dau (a Glottolog language), with new language nodes Fijian, Namosi-Naitasiri-Serua, Lauan and Lomaiviti and a dialect node Kadavu; a communalect has a Glottocode only where Glottolog 5.4 has a languoid of the same name (11) or it is one of the three Kadavu communalects. Reflexes in IPA as in the Nadrogā inventory of Lynch et al. (2002).
alternatives: 1. Proto-Fijian as parent_id (now a proposed parent of each, like Western Fijian). 2. Enter Table 16 (pp. 187-188), the percentage of eligible forms each change affects in 36 communalects: read here only for which communalects have the palatalization changes 4, 5 and 8; its rows for changes 12 and 25 did not agree with Table 15 as read from the image, so nothing else was taken from it. 3. Read chapters 3 and 4 for the conditions that the key abbreviates and for examples (none are entered). 4. Assign the Vanua Levu and Viti Levu communalects to Glottolog's dialects (West, Central, Northeast, Southeast Vanua Levu; Northeast, Southeast Viti Levu; Northwest Viti Levu; Nadrogaa) after chapters 6-7; the existing Nadrogā lect (nadr1235, Lynch et al. 2002) has h for *s like Tubaniwai and Baravi (Nadrogā) and may be one of them. 5. Write the prenasalized stops ᵐb ⁿd ᵑɡ. 6. Enter PEO *bw, *pw against a Proto-Eastern Oceanic with phonemes instead of POc.
